messages.author: 395bdca538bcae5d
messages.subject: Limited density variations: general question
parts:
I'm wondering if there is any general advice for fixing models that have really limited density variations and are demonstrating random walk behavior. Michael lays out the problem really well in this paper, but RMHMC isn't available yet.

I ask because I have a GLMM with ~500 random effects, where both the centered and noncentered form have really low Neff/N for one hypervariance in particular. The NUTS criteria look good -- no divergences at 0.8 and reasonably low tree depths. The issue appears to be that a trajectory can only traverse a really small portion of the marginal distribution for the hypervariance.

Is there any general advice for dealing with a situation like this? Or maybe something else is going on in the model that I'm missing (see attached if interested).

Thanks,
Cole

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Limited density variations: general question
parts:
On Wednesday, August 17, 2016 at 2:29:45 PM UTC-4, Cole Monnahan wrote:
Is there any general advice for dealing with a situation like this? Or maybe something else is going on in the model that I'm missing (see attached if interested).

We have had really good success with reparameterizing the X matrix of a GL{M}M in terms of its QR factors; i.e. if X = Q * R run the model with Q in place of X and then multiply the coefficients on Q by the inverse of R after-the-fact. This is semi-automatic in rstanarm, just change

fit <- glmer(toF ~ State + Pods + (1 | PlantID) + (1 | Year) + (Pods-1 | PlantID),
             family = binomial, data = flowers)

to

library(rstanarm)
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
fit <- stan_glmer(toF ~ State + Pods + (1 | PlantID) + (1 | Year) + (Pods-1 | PlantID), family = binomial,
                  data = flowers, QR = TRUE, prior = NULL)

or do it yourself with rstan.

Ben

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Limited density variations: general question
parts:
This reparameterization resolves slow sampling due to linear correlations,
not the nonlinear correlations that can limit density variation, but it has
worked wonders for me on models with non identified effects and is definitely
worth trying.

This is really interesting. I fixed a bug in my noncentered application and it is mixing MUCH better now.

I ran a quick comparison against the rstanarm code you posted and got this:

model minESS time ESS.per.time
noncentered 70.1 135 0.52
rstanarm 92.2 455 0.202

 So it's mixing better but taking much longer. Is this what you'd expect? I had to switch prior=NULL with prior=normal() due to an error.

I haven't looked any deeper and would be willing to if you think it's worth it. The code used to make table is below. 

Thanks,
Cole

noncentered.fit <-
  stan(file='wildflower_nc.stan', data=data, init=inits, pars=pars, chains=1)
noncentered.sims <- extract(noncentered.fit, permuted=FALSE)
noncentered.ess <- monitor(noncentered.sims, print=FALSE)[, 'n_eff']
noncentered.time <- sum(get_elapsed_time(noncentered.fit))
noncentered.df <- data.frame(model='noncentered', minESS=min(noncentered.ess),
           time=noncentered.time,
           ESS.per.time= min(noncentered.ess)/noncentered.time)


## rstanarm code from Ben Goodrich; modified slightly
## https://groups.google.com/d/msg/stan-users/LRnibbozy_w/mVE64492AAAJ
flowers <- as.data.frame(data[c('year', 'plant', 'stage', 'Pods', 'toF')])
rstanarm.fit <- stan_glmer(toF ~ stage + Pods + (1 | plant) + (1 | year) + (Pods-1 | plant), family = binomial,
                  data = flowers, QR = TRUE, prior = NULL, chains=1)
rstanarm.fit2 <- rstanarm.fit$stanfit
rstanarm.sims <- extract(rstanarm.fit2, permuted=FALSE)
rstanarm.ess <- monitor(rstanarm.sims, print=FALSE)[, 'n_eff']
rstanarm.time <- sum(get_elapsed_time(rstanarm.fit2))
rstanarm.eff <- min(rstanarm.ess)/rstanarm.time
rstanarm.df <- data.frame(model='rstanarm', minESS=min(rstanarm.ess),
           time=rstanarm.time,
           ESS.per.time= min(rstanarm.ess)/rstanarm.time)
print(rbind(noncentered.df, rstanarm.df), digits=3)
